items.title: Hassett Says CPI Data Shows Inflation Needs ‘Some Work’
items.excerpt: (Bloomberg) -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said prices have been falling for items such as beef and eggs, though consumer price data for September shows overall inflation continues to need policy attention. "If you look at the previous three months, it looked like inflation was completely under control, and now it looks like it's sort of back needing some work," Hassett told CNBC Monday. Data last week showed consumer prices advanced in September at the fastest pace in five months and a gauge of underlying price pressures rose by more than expected. The consumer price index rose 0.6% from a month earlier while a key measure of underlying price pressures, which excludes food and energy, was up 0.3%. "This is either a sort of break from the downtrend or a blip," Hassett said in the interview. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh last week did nothing to dispel market expectations that the central bank will hold interest rates steady when it meets at the end of the month. In a moderated discussion at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, Warsh made no remarks on monetary policy or his outlook for the US economy, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability. Hassett said he respects the central bank's independence and said Warsh will "do what he thinks is the right thing."

October 20, 2026 | 6:06 pm ## Ziv, VVINK release collaboration PRODUCER, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Ziv has teamed up with rising P-pop girl group VVINK for “Trisikulo,” a pop track on the familiar third-wheel experience. Released under Sony Music Entertainment, it is built around Filipino wordplay that links a tricycle’s three wheels to the feeling of being the extra person in someone else’s love story. The song was co-written by Ziv alongside Paolo Benjamin Guico of Filipino folk-pop band Ben&Ben and Angelika Samantha Ortiz, one of the songwriters behind BINI’s hit “Pantropiko.” The mixing was also done by Jacques Jenkins and mastering by Luna Tebbs. The track is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## *Love in Disguise* premieres on Prime Video *LOVE in Disguise*, a Korean series based on the hit web novel *Why Don’t You Know It’s a Girl?*, has premiered on Prime Video. It is directed by Park Dhan-hee and stars Yim Si Wan, Seorina, Kim Junghyun, and Yeonwoo. The genre-blending romance is exclusively seen on Prime Video in the Philippines and in more than 240 countries and territories worldwide. ## Estelle Fly drops club-pop single SINGAPOREAN pop artist Estelle Fly has released “Shut It Down,” a playful club-pop single about switching off the overthinking and making the dance floor your own. Inspired by the Rihanna and Kesha songs, the new release is an invitation to let loose, dance with friends and have fun even when life feels complicated. It is out now on all digital music streaming platforms. ## Cayabyab, APO, Mitch Valdes reunion THIS holiday season, National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, OPM legends APO, and performer Mitch Valdes will come together for *naRyan nAPO Kami*, the fourth chapter of the MaestroClass Concert Series. The shows will be held on Dec. 4, 5, and 6 at the Proscenium Theater at Rockwell Center, Makati. All shows take place at 7:30 p.m. Joined by the Ryan Cayabyab Singers, the special Christmas chapter of the concert series brings together familiar songs, stories, and artists in a celebration that captures the warmth and spirit of a Filipino family gathering. Tickets are available directly at the Proscenium Theater website via *https://prosceniumtheater.com/* and at the Power Plant Mall Cinema. ## *Amir* gets international distribution GMA Pictures, GMA Public Affairs, and Brightburn Entertainment have officially locked in a partnership deal with Columbia Pictures for the distribution of the upcoming fantasy-drama film and 52 nd Metro Manila Film Festival (MMFF) finalist *Amir*. It is directed by Zig Dulay, with a script crafted by National Artist for Film and Broadcast Arts Ricky Lee alongside Anj Atienza. The film’s cast features Dennis Trillo, Argus Aspiras, Glaiza de Castro, Will Ashley, Caprice Cayetano, Epy Quizon, Joel Saracho, Ronnie Lazaro, Laila Ulao, Heath Jornales, Yasser Marta, Mad Ramos, Ethan Hariot, Hebron Ecal, and Mon Confiado. ## Rachel Chinouriri releases new album UK’s indie-pop singer-songwriter Rachel Chinouriri has released her second studio album, I think I spoke too soon, via Atlas Artists/Parlophone Records. The album expands upon the pop, indie, and rock influences that Ms. Chinouriri has long used to sketch portraits of her inner world. The album’s focus track is “Pretty girls,” which celebrates women, self-confidence, and the freedom to express oneself without fear of judgement. ## M2M 2027 world tour has Manila leg NORWEGIAN pop duo M2M have announced that their global tour *TWO* will be coming to Manila in 2027. The tour will start in March and after concerts at Mexico, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Jakarta, M2M’s global tour will reach Manila on April 2, 2027, at the Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City. Tickets will go on sale on Oct. 24 at 10 a.m. via *TicketNet.com.ph* and TicketNet outlets nationwide. items.excerpt: NEW YORK (AP) — Beloved character actor Richard Riehle has died at 78. Wright Entertainment Inc. announced Monday that Riehle died on Oct. 15. Riehle's career spanned nearly five decades, with memorable roles in “Office Space,” “Glory,” and “The Fugitive.” He often played authority figures but was equally skilled in comedy. He began acting at the University of Notre Dame and later earned a Masters of Fine Arts from the University of Minnesota. Riehle appeared in three “Star Trek” series and on Broadway. He is remembered for his talent, kindness, and support for emerging actors. ... But DC Studios' “Clayface” is the rare attempt to meld the two movie genres. “Clayface” is something unusual in the normally calculated realm of comic book movies. It’s R-rated. It’s also modestly budgeted at $40 million. And it stars the relatively unknown Tom Rhys Harries as a little-known DC villain. And it comes at a pivotal time for James Gunn and Peter Safran's DC Studios, following the box-office flop of “Supergirl” and the Warner Bros. merger with Paramount. ... “La Bola Negra” is a Spanish flim that explores the lives of gay men in Spain in 1932, 1937 and 2017. Directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, the film draws inspiration from Federico García Lorca and Alberto Conejero’s works. It weaves stories of love, war and generational trauma, featuring a standout debut by Guitarricadelafuente. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr writes that the film, despite some stylistic weight, is a remarkably transfixing exercise and exploration of the caustic ripple effects of repression and silence. Rated R, the film is in theaters now and will be on Netflix in December.
